subject: Order Form: Liability exceptions and consequential damages definition
messages:
From: Ethan Cole <ethan.cole@grovemaps.com>
To: Priyom Das <priyom_das@redwood.com>
Cc: GroveMaps Legal <contracts@grovemaps.com>
Date: Sat, 12 Jun 2027 09:14:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Order Form: Liability exceptions and consequential damages definition

Hi Priyom —

Thanks for sending the latest order form. Our legal team flagged the liability section: they want the consequential damages carve-out to be one-way (customer only) rather than mutual, and they want a narrow definition of "consequential/special/incidental/punitive" tied to third-party claims and downstream revenue loss.

I know Redwood typically pushes for mutual exclusions. Can you outline two options we can present to our counsel: (1) mutual exclusion with a short list of carve-ins we accept, and (2) a customer-favorable one-way exclusion with a higher cap?

We're trying to keep this close so procurement can sign off next week.

Thanks,
Ethan

Ethan Cole
Director, Platform Partnerships
GroveMaps Inc.

Attachment: Grove_Redlines_Summary.txt (text summary of proposed changes)
From: Priyom Das <priyom_das@redwood.com>
To: Ethan Cole <ethan.cole@grovemaps.com>
Cc: laura_bennett@redwood.com, markus_klein@redwood.com
Date: Sat, 12 Jun 2027 12:30:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Order Form: Liability exceptions and consequential damages definition

Ethan —

Appreciate the heads-up. We're comfortable presenting both paths to GroveMaps. High-level options below (I'll pull in legal for precise wording):

1) Mutual exclusion (our preferred):
   - Both parties exclude consequential/special/incidental/punitive damages, except for (i) willful misconduct, (ii) breaches of IP indemnity, and (iii) personal injury.
   - Cap remains as negotiated on the OF (12 months of fees) except for carve-ins above.

2) One-way (customer-only) exclusion with higher cap:
   - Redwood accepts that only customer waives consequential damages; Redwood retains liability for direct damages, and retains carve-ins e.g., data breach costs, security incidents, and IP claims.
   - Cap increased to 18 months of fees or $2M (whichever is greater) to offset one-way language.

I'll ask legal to draft exact redline options and mark tradeoffs. If procurement needs the one-way path to get a signature, we can present the higher-cap tradeoff plus clarified definition that limits "consequential" to purely downstream lost profits and third-party claims.

Circling in Laura and Markus to confirm what we can offer without escalating.

- Priyom

Priyom Das | Account Executive | Redwood Inference
From: laura_bennett@redwood.com
To: Priyom Das <priyom_das@redwood.com>, markus_klein@redwood.com
Cc: monica_patel@redwood.com
Date: Sun, 13 Jun 2027 08:02:00 -07:00
Subject: RE: Order Form: Liability exceptions and consequential damages definition

Folks —

Thanks for the summary. Attached are two redline snippets (PDF) I prepared for the OF: one implementing mutual exclusion with limited carve-ins; the other implementing a customer-favorable one-way exclusion with an increased cap and explicit definition. Key legal notes below:

- Definition fight: "Consequential/special/incidental/punitive" should be tied to a non-exhaustive examples list (lost profits, lost business, reputational harm), but we must avoid language that swallows ordinary direct damages (e.g., replacement costs, remediation). We propose: "Consequential Damages means indirect, special, incidental, or punitive damages arising from loss of profits, loss of business, or other economic loss not reasonably foreseeable at the time of contracting."

- Carve-ins: we will not give up IP indemnity breaches or Redwood's obligations arising from gross negligence/willful misconduct. We should keep security/data breach costs as carve-ins when they arise from Redwood's breach of security obligations.

- Cap mechanics: If Grove insists on a one-way exclusion, we need a material economic concession — either higher cap (18 months or $2.5M) or specific SLAs with credits and a termination right after repeated breaches.

- Punitive damages: we cannot agree to an uncapped punitive liability; it must remain excluded except where law prohibits exclusion.

I'll draft clean redlines for both options and a short memo explaining the trade-offs for the AE and CSM.

Laura Bennett
Senior Counsel, Contracts | Redwood Inference
Attachment: Laura_Redlines_Mutual_vs_OneWay.pdf (2 pages)
From: GroveMaps Legal <contracts@grovemaps.com>
To: laura_bennett@redwood.com, Priyom Das <priyom_das@redwood.com>
Date: Sun, 13 Jun 2027 10:15:00 -0700
Subject: RE: Order Form: Liability exceptions and consequential damages definition

Laura/Priyom —

Thanks for the quick turnaround. A few clarifying points from GroveMaps counsel: 1) Their interest in a one-way carve-out is driven by a downstream reseller agreement that prohibits them from accepting mutual broad exclusions. 2) They are open to an increased cap and SLA-based remedies. 3) They want the definition to explicitly exclude "remediation costs reasonable incurred to restore data or services" from the consequential bucket.

They asked if Redwood can accept: "Consequential Damages do not include reasonable remediation costs to restore data or services resulting directly from Redwood's breach of this Agreement." If Redwood accepts that carve-out, Grove will consider the one-way exclusion paired with the 18-month cap.

Ethan
From: Priyom Das <priyom_das@redwood.com>
To: Ethan Cole <ethan.cole@grovemaps.com>, GroveMaps Legal <contracts@grovemaps.com>
Cc: laura_bennett@redwood.com, monica_patel@redwood.com
Date: Mon, 14 Jun 2027 09:40:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Order Form: Liability exceptions and consequential damages definition

Ethan —

Thanks — that's helpful context. Laura: can we accept the remediation carve-out language Ethan pasted without creating a hole that swallows direct damages? My read: reasonable remediation costs to restore data/services = direct remediation (good), but we still need to preserve carve-ins for security-related remediation when Redwood is at fault.

Next steps I propose:
- Laura to produce two short, marked-up OF attachments (mutual and one-way with the proposed remediation line).
- If Grove selects one-way + 18-month cap, Redwood will require SLA language: service credits up to X% per incident, and termination for repeated SLA misses.
- Monica (CSM) to prepare an SLO/SLA summary we can attach to the OF so procurement sees remediation path and operational commitments.

Can you confirm procurement timeline? Grove mentioned wanting signature next week.

Thanks,
Priyom
From: markus_klein@redwood.com
To: laura_bennett@redwood.com, priyom_das@redwood.com
Cc: monica_patel@redwood.com
Date: Mon, 14 Jun 2027 11:05:00 -07:00
Subject: RE: Order Form: Liability exceptions and consequential damages definition

Laura / team —

From a commercial standpoint I support offering the one-way exclusion only with the increased cap and tightened remediation carve-out. A couple of redline notes:

- Quantify "reasonable remediation costs" — suggest limiting to direct labor and third-party contractor fees, capped per incident (e.g., $250k) to avoid open-ended exposure.
- Add a proviso that remediation costs reimbursed under the carve-out reduce any future service credit recoveries (to avoid double recovery).
- Ensure the definition specifies "losses arising from third-party downstream agreements" if Grove is asking to protect resellers. We should not be on the hook for Grove's indirect chain beyond reasonably foreseeable damages.

If Laura can produce the one-way redline with those specifics, I think we can sign off from Sales and escalate to leadership only if Grove pushes further.

-Markus

Markus Klein | Head of Sales Operations | Redwood Inference
From: laura_bennett@redwood.com
To: Ethan Cole <ethan.cole@grovemaps.com>, Priyom Das <priyom_das@redwood.com>
Cc: markus_klein@redwood.com, monica_patel@redwood.com
Date: Tue, 15 Jun 2027 10:22:00 -07:00
Subject: RE: Order Form: Liability exceptions and consequential damages definition

Ethan / GroveMaps counsel —

Please find attached our revised OF redline implementing the one-way consequential damages exclusion in Section 10 with the following guardrails:

1) Definition: "Consequential Damages" limited to indirect losses such as loss of profits or business interruption and expressly excluding direct remediation costs.
2) Remediation carve-out: Redwood accepts reimbursement for reasonable remediation costs resulting from Redwood's breach, defined as direct labor and third-party contractor fees, capped at $200,000 per incident.
3) Cap: Mutual overall liability cap is replaced (for this deal only) with a customer-favorable one-way exclusion but with Redwood's maximum aggregate liability set at the greater of $2,000,000 or 18 months of fees.
4) SLA/credits: We included a linked SLO schedule (Attachment B) with tiered credits and a termination right after three consecutive P1 misses.

If Grove can confirm acceptance of these points, I'll prepare a clean OF for signature and the DocuSign envelope.

Regards,
Laura Bennett
Senior Counsel, Contracts | Redwood Inference
